title: Employers in health, aged care and construction report persistent shortages that skilled migration helps fill
oneLiner: The government's own shortage list shows the same occupations year after year.
body: Jobs and Skills Australia's annual occupation shortage list has consistently included nurses, aged-care workers, electricians, carpenters and other trades. Employers in those sectors argue that skilled and temporary migration is the only way to staff them at current wages and training rates.
contextBackground: Shortage lists are the formal basis for skilled visa eligibility, which is why they feature in every migration debate. They record employers' reported difficulty hiring, not an independent measure of need.
contextDisagreement: That the lists say this is agreed. Whether reported shortages reflect genuine scarcity or wages set too low to attract local workers is the dispute, and it does not resolve on the data alone.

evidenceItems.citation: Jobs and Skills Australia, Occupation Shortage List

otherClaim.title: Net overseas migration should be held below 200,000 a year

claimItself.title: Net overseas migration should be held below 200,000 a year
claimItself.oneLiner: Whether the federal government should cap net arrivals below the levels of the past decade and well below the post-pandemic peak.
claimItself.body: Net overseas migration is arrivals minus departures of people who stay, or leave, for at least twelve months. It averaged just over 200,000 a year in the decade before the pandemic and exceeded 500,000 in 2022–23. The proposal is a cap of 200,000, which would require the government to manage the student, temporary-work and permanent programs together to hit it.

otherClaim.title: Permanent skilled visas make up a minority of net overseas migration; students and other temporary entrants make up most of it

claimItself.title: Permanent skilled visas make up a minority of net overseas migration; students and other temporary entrants make up most of it
claimItself.oneLiner: A cap on total net migration need not touch the skilled program at all.
claimItself.body: The permanent skilled stream is set each year in the budget and has run at roughly 130,000 to 140,000 places, many granted to people already in the country. Net overseas migration is several times larger and is driven mainly by temporary arrivals. A cap could therefore be met without reducing the skilled intake.
